key_idea: Perturbing the area functional with a prescribed mean curvature term on Caccioppoli sets forces the approximating min-max surfaces to be boundaries with multiplicity one, while a cleverly chosen global prescribing function guarantees that any higher-multiplicity limit would yield a forbidden constant-sign solution to the Jacobi equation.
reason: The proof introduces an unexpected and brilliant perturbation strategy to break the symmetry of minimal surfaces, forcefully ruling out higher-multiplicity limits via a contradiction in the Jacobi equation. Although the rigorous implementation requires the heavy technical bookkeeping of Almgren-Pitts min-max theory, the conceptual core is strikingly elegant and explanatory.
recognized: Xin Zhou, On the Multiplicity One Conjecture in Min-max theory
